rationale.conceptual: The paper applies an established but non-trivial time-dependent quantum mechanical method involving multiple coupled excited states, FFT-based wavepacket propagation, correlation functions, and Fourier transforms to predict interference effects. Implementing this requires genuine understanding of quantum dynamics, careful handling of nonadiabatic couplings, and correct translation of the mathematical formalism into working code, going well beyond a textbook operation or standard library call.
rationale.execution: The pipeline consists of several sequential stages: obtaining external potential energy data, solving vibrational eigenstates, preparing wavepackets, propagating on four coupled surfaces (16384 time steps), computing correlation functions, Fourier transforms, and output formatting. While the individual steps use standard numerical libraries (numpy/SciPy) and no exotic tooling, orchestrating the coupled-channel dynamics and ensuring correct time evolution and Fourier analysis introduces moderate complexity.
